newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds net drops on lower metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds net drops on lower metal prices.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co Tuesday reported drop in third quarter profits saying results were affected by primary aluminum prices 19 percent lower than the 1995 third quarter and fabricated product price declines.

"In addition, Reynolds experienced reduced shipping levels in our can and can sheet businesses and continued softness in Europe. This was partially offset by higher shipments in our distribution and construction products businesses," said chief executive Jeremiah J. Sheehan.
"The improvement in aluminum industry fundamentals that had been anticipated for 1996 has not materialized," he said.
"The deterioration in prices that we have experienced will make it difficult to achieve any improvement in our operating results for the balance of this year," said Sheehan.

"Reynolds has set a goal to improve pretax performance in 1997 by $100 million, or $1.00 per share, excluding the effect of price changes. All of our businesses are currently developing plans to contribute to this goal," he continued.

He said improvements and modernizations are under way in the Can and Flexible Packaging divisions, in the can stock production process, and in European rolling and extrusion operations, adding the benefits will be realized in 1997.
"We also plan to hold capital spending in 1997 to $350 million, compared to approximately $450 million in 1996," said Sheehan.

The company said third-quarter net income dropped to $26 million, or $0.26 per share, from to $112 million, or $1.56 per share, a year earlier. The latest quarter include a favorable effect of $6 million, or $0.10 per share, from LIFO inventory liquidations.
It said inventories have been reduced $141 million from a year ago and $54 million in 1996.

Revenues in the latest period were $1.76 billion, compared to $1.85 billion in the 1995 third quarter. Aluminum shipments were 420,000 metric tons, compared to 428,000 metric tons in the 1995 third quarter.
For the first nine months of the year, Reynolds reported net income of $88 million, or $0.95 per share, compared to $305 million, or $4.20 per share, in 1995.

The 1996 results are after charges of $38 million, or 60 cents per share, for the effects of an accounting change and restructuring charges recorded in the first quarter. The 1996 results also include a favorable effect of $9 million, or $0.15 per share, from LIFO inventory liquidations.
Nine-month revenues were $5.27 billion, compared with $5.38 billion in 1995. Aluminum shipments were 1,235,000 metric tons, compared with 1,246,000 metric tons in 1995.
